record.original_question: A function f analytic in D, is said to be annular if there exists a sequence {Jn } of Jordan curves in D such that (a) Jn lies in the inside of Jn+1 , (b) for each positive ε there exists a number N (ε) such that for if n > N (ε), Jn lies in the domain {z : 1 − ε < |z| < 1}, (c) min{|f (z)| : z ∈ Jn } → ∞ as n → ∞. Let T denote the unit circle and let Z ′ (f ) denote the set of limit points of the zeros of an annular function f . Write S(f ) = {a : a ∈ C and Z ′ (f − a) 6= T }, and let |S(f )| denote the cardinality of this set. Can |S(f )| = N0 ? The cases |S(f )| = 1 (Barth and Schneider [65]) and |S(f )| = 2 (Osada (no citation)) are known, however neither construction can be easily adapted to the general case. (K. F. Barth and D. D. Bonar)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc and $\mathbb{T}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|=1\}$ the unit circle. A function $f$ analytic in $\mathbb{D}$ is called annular if there exists a sequence $\{J_n\}$ of Jordan curves in $\mathbb{D}$ such that:
(a) $J_n$ lies in the interior of $J_{n+1}$ for every $n$;
(b) for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $N(\varepsilon)$ such that for all $n>N(\varepsilon)$, $J_n$ is contained in the annulus $\{z:1-\varepsilon<|z|<1\}$;
(c) $\min\{|f(z)|:z\in J_n\}\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$.

For an annular function $f$, let $Z'(f)$ denote the set of limit points (in $\overline{\mathbb{D}}$) of the zero set of $f$. Define
$$S(f)=\{a\in\mathbb{C}:Z'(f-a)\neq\mathbb{T}\}.$$

It is known that there exist annular functions $f$ for which $|S(f)|=1$ and annular functions for which $|S(f)|=2$.

Question: Does there exist an annular function $f$ such that $|S(f)|=\aleph_0$ (i.e., $S(f)$ is countably infinite)?
artifact.category_tag: annular functions in the unit disc
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned related work by Barth, Bonar, and Carroll on zeros and Fatou points of annular and strongly annular functions, but no source was found that resolves whether $|S(f)|$ can equal $\aleph_0$ for an annular function. The status of this specific question could not be verified.
